method: Y-tube olfactometer (10 cm stem, 15 cm arms, 1.5 cm inner diameter), compound against liquid paraffin control, chi-square tests; the sentence follows head-to-head comparisons of single compounds at set concentrations (Figure 6A)
conditions: newly emerged laboratory-reared adult females (colony founded from field insects at Danzhou), starved 3 h, 26 C and 75% RH; 60 females per compound concentration; arms swapped after every 10 insects (randomisation not described); beta-bisabolene against control: 10 ug/uL chi2 = 9.000, p = 0.003, 100 ug/uL chi2 = 4.000, p = 0.046, with no preference at 0.01, 0.1 and 1 ug/uL; 3-ethylbenzaldehyde and nonanal gave no preference at any concentration; the same section reports no significant difference between methyl salicylate and either 1,3-diethenylbenzene or trans-cinnamaldehyde, and that 1,3-diethenylbenzene at 100 ug/uL beat trans-cinnamaldehyde (chi2 = 5.760, p = 0.016); the authors' EAG sentence says all six compounds gave dose-dependent responses, but methyl salicylate showed no significant EAG difference at 0.01 to 10 ug/uL (F = 2.163, p = 0.089), so the compounds are not equal in EAG; the olfactory responses are attraction in a walking assay, not thresholds
